input.task: Open the partner site and read its heading.

provenance: cold review of M4, finding 1. The guard was consulted in exactly two places — the submitted URL string at the gateway, and the `navigate` branch of execute() — so a CLICK that leaves the allowed host was never checked, nor was a 302 or meta-refresh, nor the final_url the run reports. The frontend told reviewers verbatim that a blocked URL is refused before a browser opens, which was true only of the string. Worse, no eval ever passed url_guard into run_task at all: both in-agent guard checks could be deleted and every suite stayed green. Watched red by deleting the post-action guard check: the click then navigated onto the blocked URL unchallenged and the run carried on there, ending failure:locate on an ambiguous heading several steps later. Worth stating precisely — the observable damage is not a wrong answer, it is that the browser was somewhere the guard exists to forbid and nothing noticed; what it did next was incidental.

triage.note: uses an injected marker predicate (`block_host`) rather than the production url_ok, because the fixtures are served on loopback and the real guard blocks loopback — passing url_ok into a fixture case would fail every case for the wrong reason. So this grades the ENFORCEMENT (the guard is consulted whenever the browser changes host), while url-guard-literal-ips grades the PREDICATE. Neither is coverage without the other.
